angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 473,772 km at 62.00 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 16.1303 +/- 0.0176 mas (same row, RUWE 1.29): 62.00 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.681 +/- 0.018 solar radii from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-141 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract): 473,772 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.708 +/- 0.028 solar masses from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-141 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4570 +/- 100 K from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-141 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-141 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-141.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.622, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-141 (pscomppars): spectral type K7 V, from Barragán et al. 2018 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A&A...612A..95B/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, StKM 1-2122: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-141 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0 dex, from Bonomo et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-141 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.75, from Malavolta et al. 2018 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155..107M/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-141 (pscomppars): age 6.3 Gyr, from Bonomo et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-141 (pscomppars): rotation period 15.17 d, from Bonomo et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract)

rotationPeriodsCatalogued.source: VizieR J/ApJ/890/L31/table1 (Rotational periods and J_2_ of Kepler stars), column Prot: 7 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place

projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-141 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 3 km/s, from Barragán et al. 2018 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A&A...612A..95B/abstract)
rotationPeriodMeasuredSource: Measured in this project from the K2 mission's own light curve of campaign 12 (packages/telescope-cli/src/archives/tess/reduce.mts), by the method and criteria of Reinhold & Hekker (2020, A&A 635, A43): 14.02 d, the light swinging by 1.1% as the star turns (the light repeats every 7.01 d, half the catalogued rotation period, and the star is taken to turn once in two of them)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
